resources.string: *Touch a square* on the board to aim there.\nYou can slide your finger to another one.\n*Lift your finger* to fire!
*Touch a piece* in line with the gap\nto slide it over, or *drag it* toward the gap.\nWhole rows move along!
*Touch the slot* with the letter\'s sign\nto sort it there!
*Drag* across the screen to aim the cannon.\n*Tap* to fire!
*Tap anywhere* on the screen\nto raise your bid!
To answer, just *touch the line*\nyou want to say.
*Swipe up or down* to change a digit,\n*left or right* to pick another one.\n*Tap* when the number is right!
*Touch an item* to take a closer look.\n*Touch it again* to buy it!
*Drag* to turn the figure around.\n*Pinch* with two fingers to look closer!
Hold a finger on the *left half* for the beat:\nleft for 4/4, right for 6/4, none for 3/4.\n*Drag on the right half* to conduct!
*Right pad*: tap or slide to a note sign\nto swing the baton that way.\n*Left pad*: tap the time (4/4, 3/4, 6/4)!
*Drag the blue arrow* around the compass\nto choose where the wind blows.\nThen tap the *green button*!

Gliding: *tap the leaf's button*
to close the leaf and drop; tap it again
while falling to glide on.
*Hold it* to wave the leaf in the air!

*Hold an item button* to choose its item
from a ring: *slide* to an item and *let go*.
A short tap uses the item as before.
Bags open as rings of their own!
Hold the *mic button* (or *L*) and sing, hum\nor whistle a song you\'ve learned.\n*Let go* when you\'re done: Link plays it!
Sing, hum or whistle a song you\'ve learned:\nthe *microphone* is listening!\nPause briefly after the *last note*.
Want to *try it* first? Hold the mic button\nand sing: you\'ll see each *note* you hit.\nLink won\'t play anything while you practise.
*%1$s* recognised!\nPlay it for real now? Then sing it\nonce more: Link plays it.
Spoils Bag and Bait Bag filled.
The Spoils Bag and Bait Bag (if missing), every kind of spoils ×99, bait and Hyoi Pears
Map, compass and boss key (this dungeon)
Map, compass and boss key for this dungeon.
Used bait and Hyoi Pears come back, spoils stay at 99
The swim meter stays full: Link never tires or sinks in deep water
Enemies fall to a single hit (bosses with their own counters excepted)
Every inventory item, light arrows, Deluxe Picto Box, power bracelets, 4 bottles, 99 arrows and bombs
Each lift-off picks one of 14 poses instead of the two jump poses
Hold its button to rise, steer with the left stick. On the same controller button as Jump anywhere the moon jump wins
On touch it has a button of its own. A controller button the game uses while playing hands that over to another one, or an item button is taken off
%1$s presses %2$s in the game. With %3$s on it as well, it would do both.
No free controller button is left for %1$s.
Take off: no controller button presses %1$s any more; its item can\'t be used from the controller (the other item buttons stay).
Take off: no controller button presses %1$s any more; the item ring still has what it did (Wind Waker, cannon, salvage arm).

Move to L1 / D-pad down: %1$s goes onto that button instead and keeps its item, its slot on the item page shows the new button. L1 then no longer presses the Wii U\'s L (no page turns there, no mic button for the songs); d-pad down stays d-pad down outside play.
Landing after a flight never hurts
Equip Master Sword and Mirror Shield
Master Sword and Mirror Shield equipped until the save file is loaded again.
Until the save file is loaded again
These change the save file you are playing (from the original project). They apply once a save file is loaded; save in the game to keep them.

This can change or break story events. Save to a spare file first. Apply it?

Adds interpolated frames between the game\'s 30 fps frames, using the frame generation of Lossless Scaling. It needs your own copy of Lossless.dll from your Lossless Scaling installation (Steam: steamapps/common/Lossless Scaling). Copy it to this device and choose it here. Generated frames show the game about one frame later.
Installed: an untested version (frames may look wrong)
×%1$d (%2$d fps: more than the display shows, no generated frames)

On Adreno GPUs the game can run on another Vulkan driver than the system\'s, for example a Mesa Turnip build or a newer Qualcomm driver. Use driver packages in the AdrenoTools format (a .zip with meta.json and the driver), as other emulators use them. A new driver applies after a restart. If the game doesn\'t start with it, the next start goes back to the system driver.
%1$s couldn\'t be loaded, so the system driver runs. The next start switches back to it.
A .zip with meta.json and the driver
The driver that came with the device
Saves a state as you play, without stopping the game, into two auto slots that take turns
Runs a short test of this device and sets the preset from it (the game restarts)
Which controller button presses which Wii U button

Choose a Wii U button, then press the controller button for it. A button that is already in use swaps places, so every Wii U button keeps one. Jump anywhere and the moon jump ask first on a button the game uses while playing. Home / Guide and holding Select always open the menu, and the menu keeps using the buttons by position.
Press the controller button for %1$s (now: %2$s).\n\nHome / Guide or Cancel keeps it as it is.

Takes over item button X, Y or R from its controller button (a jump there swaps over), with its item, the item page\'s slot and the item ring. L1 then no longer presses the Wii U\'s L: no page turns on the item page, no mic button for the songs.
D-pad down as an item button
As L1, but only while playing; in menus it stays d-pad down. On the item page: hold ZL and press d-pad down to put the item under the cursor onto it.
On the game\'s buttons and the item slots of the GamePad. Auto: A1, A2, A3 by touch, with a controller the button that presses it
Step by step: what the buttons do, a suggested layout, trying it out
No controller is connected. Connect one (or press one of its buttons) and try again.
%1$s is connected.\n\nSet it up? A few steps show what its buttons do in the game and suggest a layout, also one for Jump anywhere. All of it can be changed later at Controls › Set up controller.

%1$s

The game knows only the Wii U GamePad. Each of its buttons is pressed by one button of your controller. Which one can be changed freely, and each controller keeps its own.

While playing, the game uses every button but L and d-pad down. So Jump anywhere and the moon jump either share L (L1 / LB), or take a button from the game: what that button did then moves to L or, for an item button, is taken off.

How should the four buttons on the right work?

By position: as on the Wii U GamePad. The bottom one is the sword (the Wii U's B), the right one the action button (A). The letters on your controller then differ from the game's.

By letters: your controller's A is the game's A (action), B the sword, X and Y the item buttons A2 and A1.
Choose a starting point. Single buttons can be changed afterwards.
Every button as on the Wii U. Jump anywhere and the moon jump (when on) on L1 / LB, which the game doesn\'t use while playing.
Jump on an item button, the item off
Jump anywhere on the button of an item button (A1, A2 or A3). That item button is taken off: its item can\'t be used from the controller, the other two stay. Switches Jump anywhere on.
Jump on any button, its use to L

Jump anywhere on a button of your choice, a face button for example. What that button did in the game moves to L1 / LB, so nothing is lost. Switches Jump anywhere on. For an item button, L1 becomes that item button; the Wii U\'s L then has no controller button (page turns on the item page, the songs\' mic button).
Press the item button that should jump: %1$s (A1), %2$s (A2) or %3$s (A3).\n\nThe moon jump, while it is on, takes the same button.
Press the button that should jump, a face button for example. What it does in the game moves to L1 / LB.\n\nThe moon jump, while it is on, takes the same button.
%1$s presses the game\'s %2$s, not an item button: it can\'t be taken off.
Press the controller\'s buttons: each one lights up with what it does in the game. Hold Start / Options to finish. Single buttons: Controls › Controller buttons.
With the item ring on, a d-pad direction works too (not down, the game doesn\'t use it): the ring has the Wind Waker, the cannon and the salvage arm.
%1$s presses the game\'s %2$s, neither an item button nor a d-pad direction the item ring has: it can\'t be taken off.

No controller button presses %1$s any more (taken off for a jump while the item ring had it). Without the ring, what it did can\'t be used from the controller: give it a button at Controls › Controller buttons, or run Controls › Set up controller.

Items, hearts, infinite health… for the save file you play
A, B, X, Y, R and ZR appear when there is something to do and say what; the game\'s own button display is hidden
Hold to go on in talks
A finger held anywhere on the picture goes on through a talk\'s text by itself, page by page, and stops at a question. Off: each tap goes on once
The held talk also runs fast forward (up to 4×, as fast as this device draws)
Move, resize and hide each button; opacity and style (outline or filled)
Flexible: the sticks appear where your thumb touches (left half: movement, right half: camera)
Auto: the picture is drawn at the size it needs and the screen enlarges it, which is faster on high-resolution screens; Full: always at the screen\'s own resolution

Lowers the rendering resolution while the GPU keeps the game below its frame rate (the game slows down then), and raises it back up to the setting above when there is room. The performance overlay shows the current value
Save your game save and save states into one backup file
Resolution of the motion estimate: lower is faster
Remove Lossless.dll from the app? Frame generation is switched off until you choose it again.
The system\'s, or an installed driver package
The hearts fade out while the sword is put away and fade in when it is drawn, when Link takes damage or when he heals; the magic bar shows on its own while magic is used
Restore them from their files; an imported game save restarts the game
Frame interpolation: in-between frames from the game\'s 30 fps. Needs a fast CPU; where a frame doesn\'t fit in time it is left out and the game keeps its speed
Push the right stick (or swipe) up to look down. First person and aiming leaves the normal camera and menus as they are
Hold X, Y or R (touch or controller) to pick the item for it; a tap uses the item as before
The languages of your copy of the game; applies after a restart
Save state when leaving the app
Keeps where you were if Android closes the game while it\'s in the background
Off: these options are a page of the + menu, behind the arrow left of the items. On: the ≡ button opens them over the game, as before

Touch the game\'s picture: Sploosh Kaboom\'s squares, the picture puzzles\' pieces, mail slots, shop items, answers; aim the cannon, bid, turn figures and conduct by dragging. Off: the stick and buttons only, as in the original
Conducting shows two pads: the five note signs (the baton\'s directions, a d-pad) and the three times. Off: a finger on each half of the picture is a stick
Ladders, vines and moving along a ledge while hanging
With a stamina wheel; B or A lets go
No easing: the camera follows the stick at once

The Picto Box album gets any number of pages of 12 pictos: when it is full, a new picto starts a new page. In the album the bar at the top (or ZL / L) turns the pages. Your save keeps the page in play, the others are stored next to it
In the Picto Box album: who a picto caught, by the gallery figurine\'s name. A gold medal picto (★) is good enough for a figurine; else it says what is missing
Show a postbox the Picto Box and choose a picto: it goes to Carlov, who makes the figurine as at the Nintendo Gallery. It is put in the gallery the next day, no visit needed
The mailed figurine is in the Nintendo Gallery at once

Send a picto to Carlov at the Nintendo Gallery? He makes a figurine of it.
Hero\'s clothes or his casual clothes (the lobster shirt) at any time; a change shows as a puff of smoke. As in the story: the game decides
As on the GameCube: after a song you conduct, Link plays it once more before it takes effect (the Wii U version goes straight to the effect)
Faster (up to 4×, as fast as this device draws) while ZR (R2) is held; text boxes still wait for your button
First person on the mouse wheel
The jump button once more in the air

Name, IDs, battery, rumble, motion sensors, lights, buttons, axes

Automatic: the controller while you play with it (if it rumbles), this device while you play by touch
Widescreen, field of view, aspect ratio, TV and GamePad screens
GPU driver, VSync, recording thread, shader cache
Replay, sing into the microphone, play buttons
Cemu graphic packs and game file mods, imported from .zip and .rar files
Controller: hold Select or press Home to open and close · L / R switch tabs · D-pad moves and changes values · right button selects · bottom button goes back

With context buttons: the Picto Box\'s viewfinder fills the screen, pinch to zoom (also the telescope). Off: the game\'s original Picto Box and telescope screens
Sets rendering resolution, dynamic resolution and frame rate together (with frame generation on: 30 fps doubled, higher resolutions). Changing one of them by hand makes it Custom
A second CPU thread prepares the GPU work: faster on most devices, slower on some (e.g. Snapdragon 855)
Each frame waits for the screen\'s refresh. Turn it on if the picture stutters badly or turns into a slideshow on your device; it may add a little input lag. Off: only with frame generation

Try the new touch controls?

The sticks appear where your thumbs land (on the right the camera turns by swiping), buttons show up only when they do something and say what, items are aimed and shot by tapping, and holding an item button opens a ring of all your items. Minigames are played by touching the picture.

Everything can be changed later under Controls; Classic brings back the fixed on-screen GamePad.
Jump whenever you like? A button of its own makes Link jump from standing or running, as off a ledge. (Mods › Jump anywhere)
And a second jump in the air?

Time without the right stick, or running towards the camera
While he runs and the right stick is left alone
Swipes turn the camera this much faster while Link sails. The telescope and other first-person views stay as they are

The first time a minigame or a menu of the game is played by touch, a message explains how. On again: every hint shows once more

ZL when the target is defeated

Imports mods from .zip and .rar files: Cemu graphic packs (for example from GameBanana or GitHub) and plain game file mods (a content folder). Code patches (patch_*.asm), game file replacements, pixel shader replacements and texture filtering rules work; vertex shaders and texture resolution rules don\'t yet. A code patch only applies to the game version it was made for. Turning packs on or off, or changing their settings, takes effect after a restart.
Delete this pack from the device?
Patch groups: %1$d for this game version, %2$d for others
Pick one or more .zip or .rar files
Changes apply after a restart; changed code is then recompiled (a short compile, or none for a combination used before).

After turning on a pack that patches code, start from the title screen once and load your quest log there: the pack sets itself up while the game loads. Save states made without the pack don\'t have it set up.

A preset is the story part of a save (items, hearts, songs, chart, each place\'s switches and chests, story flags) plus a place. Warping to it loads that story into the game you are playing; your save file only changes if you save in the game. Presets stay on this device.
%1$s\n\nWarp there with this story? It replaces the story of the game you are playing until you load your save again.
Load the story of a save file or a saved moment and warp to its place
The story just before a song is learned, Link right in front of its stone tablet or teacher

Each loads the built-in story preset from just before that song is learned and puts Link in front of where the game teaches it (a stone tablet, Tott). Read the tablet or talk to the teacher, then take out the Wind Waker when the game asks for the song.

Which version of the place loads; Story picks it from your progress
Reading the places from your game files… (a few seconds, only this once)

resources.string:
The game files were not found or don't match this build.

This app contains only the recompiled code built from your own copy of the game; it needs the extracted game files from the same dump. Extract them on a computer (see README.md: tools/wudextract.py), then copy the resulting folder (with code/, content/ and meta/ inside) to:

%1$s

For example: adb push game /sdcard/Android/data/org.wwhdrecomp.app/files/

Problem: %2$s

Welcome!

This app contains no game files. It plays your own copy of The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD for Wii U (USA, European or Japanese version).

Put these three files on this device, then choose them together:
• your disc image (.wux or .wud)
• its disc key (the image's name with .key)
• the console's common key (common.key)

Or choose a Cemu archive of your game (.wua); it needs no keys.

The app then extracts the game files (about 1.7 GB) and prepares the game code for this device. That happens once and takes a while, depending on the device's processor.
The game files found don\'t work: %1$s
Extract from your disc image or .wua…

Choose your disc image, its disc key and the console\'s common key together (long-press the first, then tap the others):
%1$s the image (.wux or .wud) %2$s its disc key (the image\'s name with .key) %3$s common.key
Or a Cemu archive of your game (.wua).
If the picker doesn\'t show your files, put them directly into Download and open Downloads there.
A key file must hold 16 bytes or 32 hex digits.
Extracting the game from your disc image…
This step needs about %1$d MB of free storage; %2$d MB are free. Free up some space and try again.

Preparing the game code for this device…\n\nThis happens once and takes a while, depending on this device\'s processor: a few minutes on fast devices, longer on slower ones. You can leave the app meanwhile: it continues in the background (see the notification), and if it is closed, it continues where it stopped.
Dividing the game code into parts (%1$d:%2$02d)
Preparing the game code was cancelled. It continues where it stopped when you start again.

Choose a backup made with Export (WindWakerHD backup ….zip), a GameCube Wind Waker save (.gci, USA, Europe or Japan: it becomes your game save, all three quest logs), or the files themselves together (long-press the first, then tap the others): cking.sav with the other cking….sav files of a game save, slot1–5.bin and .png of save states. If the picker doesn\'t show them, put the files directly into Download and open Downloads there.
GameCube save %1$s, converted: all three quest logs
No game save (cking.sav) or save states (slot1–5.bin) among the files picked.
Save states imported. States from another build of the app can\'t be loaded.
Game save imported. The game restarts now to use it (the previous save is kept in save-before-import).

Lossless.dll is installed and frame generation is on, but this version of its shaders hasn\'t been tested with the app: generated frames may look wrong. If they do, select another Lossless.dll (the README names the tested one).

On this GPU (%1$s), frame generation can make the GPU hang. The game may crash, and in rare cases the whole device may freeze or restart.\n\nIf the game crashes, the dialog at its next start offers to start without frame generation.
Lossless.dll is ready and frame generation is on.
Drag to move · tap elsewhere when done

A short test (about 2 minutes) finds the graphics settings for this device. The game starts for it, but its picture stays hidden and there is no sound. Your saves are not touched. Afterwards you choose whether to use the result.
Frame generation: if you own Lossless Scaling (Steam) and want frame generation, choose its Lossless.dll now, so the test includes it.
It stopped at: %1$s. Your settings stay as they were. You can run it again under Options > Graphics.
the app left the screen (screen off or another app) while measuring
%1$s: 60 fps, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
%1$s: 30 fps, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
%1$s with frame generation: 30 fps doubled to 60, rendering resolution up to %2$s× (lowered when needed)
Frame generation didn\'t reach 60 fps on this device, so the recommendation is without it.
The game stopped while the test tried frame generation, so it is not recommended on this device.
Patches the game code of this game version
Made for another game version: does nothing here
Your mod pack changes only take effect after a restart. Restart the game now? Progress since your last save is lost.
The game uses the new language after a restart.
Finding the game\'s shaders in your game files… (only this once)
No used Wind Waker save slots found in this file
Loaded; Auto waits for the cutscene / dialogue to end (at most 20 s)
Warp, or rate and go on with ✓ / ✗
No end after %1$.0f s: stuck. Restart the app (it is written down and skipped).
Not taken: a scene change was under way. Tap Warp again.
Applied once a save file is loaded; save in the game to keep it.
The setting applies after a restart.
The driver package couldn\'t be installed: %1$s
this is not a driver package (a .zip with meta.json and the driver\'s .so file)
%1$s is installed. Use it now? The game restarts.

The game closed last time because the phone's GPU driver hung:
%1$s

This can happen with buggy system drivers. A Turnip driver usually runs the game. Choose a driver package (a .zip in the AdrenoTools format, e.g. a recent Turnip build for your Adreno) to use it from now on, or start the game as it is.

The game closed last time because the installed GPU driver hung:
%1$s

Go back to the system driver, choose another driver package, or start the game with this one again.
Switch to %1$s? The game restarts; the first start with another driver compiles its pipelines again and takes longer.
This driver is in use. Remove it and restart with the system driver?
The game didn\'t start with the GPU driver %1$s, so it runs on the system driver again. You can choose the driver again under Graphics › GPU driver.

A crash log was saved. If you report the problem (for example as an issue on GitHub), please attach it. It shows where the game crashed, the app version, the game version, your device model and the settings in use. It contains no personal data.

The game restarts without its shader cache, as on the first start: shaders are compiled again as scenes appear, so the first visit to each scene loads slower and may stutter. Saves, save states and settings stay. (Unsaved progress is lost.)
Drag to move (locks on the grid while Grid is on), pinch or Size to resize, tap to select.
Opacity: only the selected control (tap an empty spot for all)
Opacity: all controls (tap a control for only that one)
No saved layouts yet. Save current keeps the layout you are editing under a name.
A layout for the %1$s touch controls. Load puts it into the editor; Done keeps it.
A saved layout of this style already has this name. Replace it?
This layout is for the %1$s touch controls. Load it and switch the touch controls to %1$s?
Flexible layout: the sticks appear where your thumbs land
The bow, boomerang, hookshot and grappling hook with the context buttons. Tap: a tap aims, then the button shoots with each tap, ZL switches the view, B puts the item away. Hold: as in the game

With Item buttons: Tap, while an item is aimed only its Shoot button, B (put away), ZL and ZR (arrow types) show; the other item buttons, A, +, first person, the d-pad and the jump buttons hide, so no stray tap lets go of a drawn arrow
While Link holds the Wind Waker, sing, hum or whistle one of its songs into the microphone and he plays it (only songs he has learned). The sound is only analysed, never recorded

Hold the mic button at the bottom left (or L on a controller) while singing; letting go plays the song at once. The switch below it picks the time (3/4, 4/4, 6/4): while you hold the button, Link conducts the notes you sing, one per beat of the metronome. Off: the microphone listens by itself and a short pause ends a song
Play buttons in the song list
While Link holds the baton, + shows the songs he knows: a play button beside each one plays it at once, no conducting needed
When the story waits for one song (learning it at a stone tablet, a sage), a play button on the message box plays it at once, learned or not
Hold the mic button and sing
Without the microphone permission the songs can\'t be heard. You can allow it in the system settings of the app.
